text: In this paper we study the effect of regularization on the generalization of deep neural networks trained with small batches, which is a question of central importance in modern statistical learning theory. We introduce a family of stochastic update rules and analyze their convergence properties under mild assumptions on the loss surface, paying particular attention to the interaction between batch size and step size. Our theoretical results are complemented by experiments on standard image classification benchmarks, where the proposed method achieves competitive accuracy while requiring significantly fewer gradient evaluations than the baselines we compare against. We further show that the benefit of the method is largest in the low-data regime, which is common in many scientific applications where annotated examples are expensive to collect. All experiments are reproducible with the code we release alongside this work, and we discuss the practical implications of our findings for practitioners.

We study the practical limits of end-to-end fine-tuning for small language models in low-resource settings, where labeled examples are scarce and hardware budgets are tight. Our setup uses a fixed budget of annotated examples and compares several parameter-efficient adaptation strategies under controlled conditions. We find that simple LoRA configurations match full fine-tuning on most tasks while using a fraction of the memory.
